device.description: 12-bit single-channel voltage-output DAC with internal reference, serial shift-register input, load strobe and asynchronous clear
device.note: dac7611.pdf (SBAS075, Burr-Brown PDS-1402A) p.2 specifications (VDD 4.75-5.25 V, TTL inputs, straight binary), p.3 pin configuration and descriptions (DIP/SOIC-8), p.5 timing diagrams, logic truth table and timing specifications, p.10 operation and interface (double buffered, LD transparent latch, CLR to 000H)

registers.name: SR
registers.note: serial shift register (p.5 truth table, p.10); power-on value not specified

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: DAC register, a transparent latch while LD is low (p.3, p.10); power-on value not specified, CLR sets 000H

commands.name: Shift D11-D0
commands.note: p.5 timing / p.10: 12 bits MSB first on rising CLK while CS is low; the shift register keeps the last 12 bits

pages: p.2 (VDD, logic levels, data coding), p.3 (pins, ordering), p.5 (timing, truth table), p.10 (interface, LD, CLR)
notModeled: analog output and internal 2.435-V reference (output never driven)
the shift register is updated bit by bit: with LD low the DAC register follows each new bit; the model writes the shift-register value when CS rises (then LD low copies it at once)
CS and CLK are interchangeable (the shift clock is CS OR CLK); the model shifts only on CLK edges while CS is low
CLR loads 000H into the DAC register only (the shift register keeps its data and LD low after CLR reloads it); the model clears both registers
power-on register contents are not specified (modeled as 0); the datasheet recommends CLR at power-up
TTL logic levels (VIH 2.4 V, VIL 0.8 V)
variants: DAC7611 has its own datasheet; DIP packages (P suffix) are not in the parts list. DAC7612 is the dual version with 2 address bits and no CLR; DAC8512 is the pin-compatible original
